questions.question: Where were the famous Judean balsam shrubs cultivated?
options: In guarded gardens near Jericho and along the Dead Sea, including Ein Gedi
On the hills around Nazareth
In the Temple courts of Jerusalem
On the coast near Caesarea
questions.explanation: Pliny, Josephus, Strabo, and Dioscorides describe guarded balsam gardens near Jericho and along the Dead Sea, including Ein Gedi.

questions.question: What happened to the balsam plantations after the war of 66–70 AD?
options: They were burned and never replanted
They became imperial income
They were given to the Essenes
They were moved to Egypt
questions.explanation: After the war of 66–70 AD the plantations became imperial income. A century later Galen still travelled to learn the drug on the spot.

questions.question: Which five plants does the Bible itself name as medicines?
options: Garlic, onion, cumin, dill, and mint
Wine, honey, oil, salt, and vinegar
Myrrh, frankincense, aloes, cassia, and cinnamon
Fig, nard, hyssop, balm of Gilead, and mandrake
questions.explanation: Only fig, nard, hyssop, balm of Gilead, and mandrake are named as medicines in the Bible. Many more plants were used.

questions.question: In Leviticus 13–15, who inspects a skin disease for color, depth, and spread?
options: A Greek physician
A midwife
A priest
A root-cutter
questions.explanation: Leviticus is priestly, not Hippocratic. A priest inspects the skin, quarantines, re-examines, and declares the person clean.

questions.question: What did the mikveh mark, according to the chapter?
options: Return to the community after impurity
Treatment for rheumatism with hot water
A Roman-style bath with a hot room
A place to buy balsam
questions.explanation: The mikveh, a pool of “living” water, marked return to the community. It is not a Roman therma.
